title: Car Fleet
algorithm: Sort by Position + Stack Arrival Times
oneLinerQuestion: Determine how many car fleets will arrive at a target destination.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Car Fleet problem asks how many car fleets will arrive at the destination target given N cars at initial positions traveling at individual speeds. A car cannot pass another car ahead of it; when a faster trailing car catches up to a slower leading car, it slows down to match its speed and merges into the same fleet. Because cars cannot overtake one another, fleet formations are determined strictly by the behavior of cars closer to the destination. By sorting the cars in descending order of starting position, we process them from front to back (closest to `target` first). The arrival time for each car is calculated as `(target - position) / speed`. If a trailing car reaches the destination in equal to or less time than the car ahead of it, it will inevitably catch up before or at the target line, coalescing into the leading fleet. Otherwise, it establishes a new, independent fleet behind it.

- Step 1: Pairwise Aggregation & Descending Position Sort — We bundle each car's position and speed into a pair `[position[i], speed[i]]` and sort these pairs in descending order based on initial position: `pairs.sort((a, b) => b[0] - a[0])`. This ensures we evaluate leading cars before trailing cars.

- Step 2: Stack or Monotonic Tracker Initialization — We initialize a stack (or a scalar variable `prevTime = 0` and counter `fleets = 0`) to track the arrival times of distinct fleet leaders: `const stack = []`.

- Step 3: Sequential Traversal & Arrival Time Computation — We iterate through each sorted pair `[pos, spd]`. For each car, we compute its unimpeded time to arrive at the target: `const time = (target - pos) / spd`.

- Step 4: Fleet Membership Evaluation via Monotonic Condition — We push the computed `time` onto `stack`. If `stack.length >= 2`, we compare the current car's time with the fleet ahead of it: if `stack[stack.length - 1] <= stack[stack.length - 2]`, the trailing car catches up and merges into the preceding fleet, so we discard the trailing car's arrival time via `stack.pop()`.

- Step 5: Independent Fleet Preservation — If `stack[stack.length - 1] > stack[stack.length - 2]`, the trailing car takes strictly longer to arrive than the car ahead of it and can never catch up, forming a new fleet leader.

- Step 6: Termination & Fleet Count Return — Once all cars have been evaluated, each entry remaining in `stack` represents an independent car fleet reaching the target. We return `stack.length`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N log N) where N is the number of cars, dominated by sorting the positions and speeds (the subsequent linear sweep runs in O(N) time). Space Complexity: O(N) auxiliary space to store the car pairs and the monotonic stack (or O(1) extra space excluding the sorted pairs by tracking only the maximum leading fleet time).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION carFleet(target, position, speed):
    pair = [[p, s] FOR p, s IN ZIP(position, speed)]
    SORT(pair BY position DESCENDING)
    stack = EMPTY_STACK()
    FOR p, s IN pair DO:
        PUSH (target - p) / s TO stack
        IF LENGTH(stack) >= 2 AND TOP(stack) <= SECOND_TOP(stack) THEN POP(stack)
    END FOR
    RETURN LENGTH(stack)
END FUNCTION
